source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-3

procedures.title: Dry charge battery: activate
steps: After the first fill, recheck the level in every cell.
If a level has dropped below the split vent, top it up with more electrolyte.
Never use water when activating the battery.
notes: Poor activation leads to poor performance and short battery life.
Once filled, the battery is a wet charged battery and is maintained like any other wet battery.

procedures.title: Battery: diagnosing failure when it tests good
steps: Check whether accessories were left on overnight (discharged battery).
Check whether electrical load exceeds generator capacity.
Check the charging system for high resistance, a slipping fan belt, or a faulty generator or regulator.
Look for abuse: dirty battery top, dirty or loose clamps and posts, wrong water additions.

procedures.title: Battery electrolyte level: check
steps: Look at the level indicator in the second cell cap from the positive post: a dark rod top means the level is fine; a glowing top means water is needed (see figures 5b and 6b in the manual).
When the indicator shows low, check all six cells.
Alternatively, remove a vent plug and look into the vent well; the level is right when the surface first distorts at the bottom of the split vent.
Check regularly, and more often in hot weather and on long trips.
If low, add colorless, odorless drinking water to each cell up to the split vent.
